About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role 
 Anthropic is hiring a Field Marketing Lead dedicated to the Public Sector Industry — one of the fastest-growing customer segments we serve, and one we believe will define how the next generation of AI-native companies adopts and builds with Claude. You will own the field marketing strategy and end-to-end execution for Public Sector audiences in the US, partnering closely with our Public Sector Sales teams. 
 This is a builder role. Field Marketing at Anthropic is a small, scrappy team and the Public Sector is an area of growth for the business — there is no existing playbook for you to inherit. You will design the event calendar, build the integrated digital programs, develop the necessary partnerships, and create the playbooks that scale across our Public Sector motion. 
 Responsibilities 
 
 Develop and activate the US Public Sector field marketing strategy end-to-end — planning, calendar, execution, and measurement. 
 Design and run public-sector-appropriate event formats — agency roundtables, mission-focused briefings, tech demo days, industry days, and executive breakfasts — that comply with government ethics and gift rules while building trusted relationships with program and procurement stakeholders 
 Plan the field calendar around the government fiscal year — building demand programs that peak ahead of federal year-end (September 30) and state budget cycles, and capitalize on use-it-or-lose-it spending windows 
 Own presence at anchor public sector events — from sponsorship strategy to speaker placement and on-site execution 
 Build co-marketing programs with the public sector channel ecosystem — distributors, resellers, systems integrators, and contract-vehicle holders — including joint events, teaming-oriented content, and partner-sourced pipeline 
 Partner closely with Public Sector Sales and BDRs on pre-event targeting, during-event engagement, and post-event follow-up to convert attention into pipeline 
 Build operational playbooks (Demo Day activation kit, hackathon kit) that the Field Marketing team can scale across regions and segments 
 Establish baseline metrics, dashboards, and ROI reporting for all Public Sector field programs 
 Be the face of Anthropic in the Public Sector ecosystem — credible with strategic partners and agencies 
 
 Minimum qualifications 
 
 Direct Public Sector-segment experience — you have built and run programs targeting the Public Sector as your primary audience, not as an enterprise field marketer who occasionally touches Public Sector 
 End-to-end ownership of field marketing events and programs, hands on in both strategy and execution - this is a 0-1 building role with very little foundation in place 
 Repeat success across multiple companies — we are looking for a pattern of impact, scaling field or demand generation programs in different environments, not a single-company tour (however strong the brand) 
 0-to-1 builder DNA — you've built a field marketing motion from scratch (or rebuilt one), and you also have scaled-company tenure that grounds you operationally 
 Tight sales alignment — you've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with AEs and BDRs on account targeting, pre-event outreach, and post-event follow-up 
 Operational rigor — you can stand up vendor management, registration, follow-up workflows, and ROI dashboards without being asked 
 Technical credibility — you can review technical event content, brief technical speakers, and hold your own with founder/CTO audiences 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 
 10+ years across Field Marketing, Demand Generation, ABM, and Events at B2B technology companies 
 Experience working inside of a Public Sector organization that went through a rapid growth phase, or a blend of Public Sectors and scaled technology companies. 
 AI/ML field marketing experience 
 Existing relationships with public sector associations and research institutions 
 Visible thought leadership in the Public Sector ecosystem or developer ecosystem 
 
 Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or Washington, D.C. office at least 2 days a week. We encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.  
 For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $400,000 USD Logistics 
 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience 
 Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience 
 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position 
 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. 
 Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. 
 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit  anthropic.com/careers  directly for confirmed position openings. 
 How we're different 
 We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. 
 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

jobs.excerpt:
At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit klaviyo.com/careers  to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny. Why This Role, Why Now 
 GTM Data Strategy & Operations stood up from scratch with no predecessor. Today the function runs on three offshore contractors and zero FTEs , managed by a single leader who is simultaneously building the agentic infrastructure, operating it in production, and driving major initiatives (hierarchy redesign, data quality assessment, vendor optimization). 
 The operating model is deliberately agentic AI–first : a multi-agent pipeline (Cartographer, Sentinel, Resolver, Reporting) handles detection, enrichment, hierarchy mapping, and conflict resolution at scale. This is not a future-state vision, these agents are live and processing enterprise account families in production today. 
 The problem: one person cannot build, operate, and extend this system while also managing strategic workstreams. The function currently covers only core Tier‑1 fields. Dozens of account, contact, and lead signals remain unaddressed. Every pipeline run, every failure diagnosis, and every offshore handoff flows through a single point of failure. 
 This role is the first onshore execution hire for an agent operator who can keep the system running, improve it, and extend detection and resolution coverage as GTM leadership prioritizes new data elements. 
 Role Summary 
 Sit between AI systems and GTM data. Operate, tune, and extend our agentic data quality pipeline (detection, enrichment, hierarchy mapping, conflict resolution) so it runs reliably, improves continuously, and expands to cover more of the data landscape. Own the handoff between automated output and human review, managing quality and throughput with our offshore team. You don’t build agents from scratch, but you run them, evaluate their output with GTM data judgment, and make them better. 
 Core Responsibilities 
 Agent Pipeline Operations 
 
 Run and monitor production pipeline sessions (Cartographer, Sentinel, Resolver) across scheduled cadences; diagnose and resolve failures (API errors, session timeouts, data anomalies) without escalating to the function lead. 
 Execute pipeline runs in Claude Claude and tmux; manage long-running batch processes; interpret logs and output to confirm data integrity before downstream handoff. 
 Maintain pipeline orchestration scripts and configuration; extend agent coverage as new data elements are prioritized by GTM leadership. 
 
 Agent Tuning & Improvement 
 
 Refine detection rules, prompt logic, and confidence thresholds based on output analysis and false-positive/negative patterns. 
 Evaluate agent accuracy by segment (Enterprise vs. MM/SMB) and recommend rule or workflow changes backed by evidence. 
 Run bake-offs (vendor vs. AI enrichment) to optimize cost, coverage, and accuracy; document results for decision-making. 
 
 Sentinel → Offshore Resolution Loop 
 
 Own the handoff between Sentinel detection output and Concentrix triage queues; define queue structure, priority tiers, and resolution instructions. 
 Monitor offshore resolution quality and throughput; refine detection rules based on patterns surfaced through triage. 
 Close the feedback loop: track resolution outcomes back to agent configuration to reduce recurring false positives and improve detection precision. 
 
 Data Quality & Enrichment Operations 
 
 Maintain ops-only staging fields; manage the promote-to-production flow with audit controls. 
 Design and run AI-assisted enrichment workflows (Clay + LLM prompts) with evidence links and confidence thresholds. 
 Monitor fill-rate, sampled accuracy, freshness, and cost-per-record by source and segment; surface vendor performance issues and recommend changes. 
 Keep data dictionaries, SOPs, and runbooks current as agents and processes evolve. 
 
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 
 GTM Systems (SFDC): field configuration, permission sets, automation, flows. 
 Data Engineering: source availability, ID mapping, lineage (no pipeline coding). 
 Reporting: define metrics and acceptance criteria; partner on dashboard requirements. 
 
 What to Expect 
 This is a triage environment, not a steady-state one. The function is young, the data has known gaps, and the work is to stabilize and extend, not maintain and optimize. You’ll be building the plane while flying it, alongside a small team that operates with high autonomy and a bias toward measurable outcomes. If ambiguity and mess energize you, this is the right fit. 
 Success Metrics (6–12 Months) 
 Pipeline Reliability 
 
 Scheduled pipeline runs execute without function-lead intervention; failure-to-resolution cycle time under 24 hours for non-blocking issues. 
 Agent coverage extended to new data elements as prioritized (measured by number of signals under active detection). 
 
 Detection & Resolution Quality 
 
 Sentinel detection precision and recall improve quarter over quarter, tracked by segment. 
 Concentrix resolution queue throughput and accuracy meet defined acceptance thresholds. 
 False-positive rate decreases through feedback-loop refinement. 
 
 Data Quality Outcomes 
 
 Tier-1 field fill-rates: Country ≥95%; Vertical ≥90% at ≥85% sampled accuracy; Revenue bands ≥90%. 
 Hierarchy coverage 65–80%+ across target segments. 
 Enterprise cost-per-record reduction of 30–40% via AI-first + selective vendor usage. 
 
 Qualifications 
 Required 
 
 3–6 years in Data Ops, Sales Ops, or GTM Ops with hands-on data quality ownership for account and contact data. 
 Proficiency with Snowflake (SQL for querying, analysis, validation) and SFDC (object model, field configuration, data flows). 
 Working experience with Claude Code or comparable LLM-based tooling in an operational (not just experimental) context. 
 Experience designing and running AI-assisted enrichment workflows (e.g., Clay + LLM prompts) and evaluating accuracy/coverage. 
 Comfort operating in a command-line environment: tmux, shell scripts, log analysis, batch process monitoring. 
 Process design mindset with a bias toward measurable outcomes; strong written communication. 
 
 Strong Plus 
 
 Experience with account/contact data vendors (D&B, ZoomInfo, Clearbit, StoreLeads) and waterfall enrichment logic. 
 Python for QA scripting, sampling, or light automation. 
 Familiarity with prompt engineering, confidence scoring, and AI guardrails (evidence capture, versioned prompts, QA sampling gates). 
 
 Tool Stack 
 
 Core: Snowflake (SQL), SFDC, Claude Code, Clay 
 Pipeline: Shell orchestration, Cartographer / Sentinel / Resolver agents 
 Enrichment: D&B, ZoomInfo, Clearbit, StoreLeads, LLM prompts 
 Nice to Have: Python, SOQL, prompt engineering frameworks 
 AI Guardrails (Expected Practice):  Confidence floors, evidence capture, versioned prompts, 10% QA sampling gates, audit-on-promote, drift alerts, and privacy/compliance checks. This role is expected to uphold and improve these practices, not just follow them.

jobs.title: GTM Enablement Manager (Technical)
jobs.excerpt:
OVERVIEW

At Apollo GraphQL, we're on a mission to make it radically easier for engineering teams to ship fast, reliable products and services on top of the world's data, powering everything from web to mobile to agentic experiences.

We're looking for a GTM Enablement Manager who enjoys translating technical concepts into language the field can use with confidence — someone who's as comfortable in a room with engineers as they are building the materials an AE needs to navigate a tricky customer conversation. This is a builder role — you'll own the strategy, content, and delivery that get our field (AEs, SEs, and CSMs) equipped to sell and support Apollo's current customers and future customers.

Reporting to the Head of Sales, you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, and Field leadership — so the work you do shows up directly in how fast the team ramps and how well we retain customers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and own our enablement strategy end-to-end, building role-based learning paths for AEs, SEs, and CSMs across self-directed learning, just-in-time delivery, micro-learning, and major learning events.

 - Partner with RevOps to define field productivity baselines and the leading indicators — ramp time, certification engagement, time-to-first-value — that connect enablement work to business outcomes, and track whether training is actually landing over time.

 - Build a new-hire onboarding program from scratch, focused on minimizing ramp time and time-to-productivity for new field ICs.

 - Lead go-to-market readiness for major product releases, working closely with Product Marketing to take their messaging and turn it into use-case narratives, competitive intelligence, and customer-facing materials the field can actually use — then own getting it into their hands and taught.

 - Act as the connective tissue between engineering and the field, translating what's shipping and why it matters into language non-technical AEs and CSMs can use with confidence in front of customers.

 - Deliver training that actually lands — not just build the content, but leading the sessions, measuring impact and effectiveness, and adjusting as needed.

 - Bring AI into how the field works, using it to speed up content creation, mine tools like Gong for field insights, and track how reps are positioning Apollo with customers — while coaching AEs and CSMs on how to use AI in their own workflows.

 - Drive alignment across teams that don't report to you, pulling input and buy-in from Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Field leadership to get assets built and adopted.

WHO YOU ARE

You sit comfortably at the intersection of technical credibility and commercial fluency — equally at home talking API architecture with an engineer and coaching an AE on how to position it to a VP of Engineering. You think of enablement as part of the go-to-market engine, not a support function on the side of it. Your goal isn't to run a training calendar — it's to make the field measurably better at their jobs.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience operating in a fast-moving, high-growth environment, where you're helping shape the playbook rather than following one.

 - Hands-on experience building and delivering enablement programs — not just managing or orchestrating other people's content.

 - Real technical fluency: you understand the API layer and can converse credibly with engineers, with familiarity with GraphQL a plus (though not required at expert level).

 - Commercial acumen: you understand how enterprise buyers (VPs of Engineering, platform leaders, CTOs/CIOs) evaluate and buy infrastructure and developer tooling, and can convert technical capability into business value language a non-technical field IC can use with confidence. Familiarity with sales methodologies like MEDDPICC and Command of the Message, and the ability to reinforce them through enablement content.

 - A proven track record of live delivery — not just content creation. You can teach a technical concept to a non-technical audience, read whether it's landing in real time, and adjust.

 - Demonstrated ownership in ambiguous environments: you've built something from scratch before, set your own priorities, and been accountable for the result.

 - Strong cross-functional influence skills: you've driven alignment and gotten things built by pulling in people who don't report to you.

 - Practical, hands-on AI fluency, not just familiarity — you've used AI as a force multiplier to get more out of your own work, and you can teach non-technical teammates to do the same.

ABOUT APOLLO

Apollo helps teams build, operate, and scale the graphs that power modern applications. If you've streamed a show, booked a trip, or read the news online, there's a good chance Apollo was working quietly behind the scenes. We support some of the largest and most sophisticated GraphQL platforms in the world.

But we're not here just to maintain the status quo. Apollo is redefining how software teams build and ship — bringing clarity, speed, and leverage to increasingly complex systems. Our platform gives teams a single, coherent way to connect clients, services, and now AI-powered experiences, without drowning in endpoints or bespoke integrations.

Just as importantly, we're building a company where ambitious people can do the best work of their careers. That means meaningful ownership, smart teammates, and tackling hard problems that actually matter. If you like moving fast, thinking deeply, and helping shape what comes next, you'll feel right at home here.

Equal Opportunity: Apollo is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a talented and diverse workforce.

Snapdocs is the trusted infrastructure for high-stakes transactions. We started in mortgage, where trust is not assumed, the work is fragmented across many parties, and the cost of mistakes is real - and are bringing that same standard of trust to other markets.

Years of automating the hardest tasks gave us something more foundational than workflow software: an AI-native platform that makes complex work easy to complete, hard to get wrong, and built to withstand scrutiny over time.

Field marketing turns that promise into tangible presence and relationships in the market by owning the programs that put Snapdocs in front of the right audiences, in the right settings, for the right reasons. You’ll turn conferences, executive programs, customer gatherings, partner activations, and account-based programs into credible brand experiences, tight relationships, and measurable commercial impact.

THE ROLE

This is a hands-on field marketing role with broad ownership. You’ll help shape where and why Snapdocs shows up, choose the programs most relevant to our audiences and business priorities, manage the details that make those programs work, and connect every program to coordinated Sales and Marketing follow-up.

Events are the primary channel, but field marketing is broader than event execution. It also includes regional programs, executive presence, customer and prospect engagement, partner programs, and account-based plays across Snapdocs’ markets. You’ll help make our mission tangible by creating experiences that simplify complexity, build trust, and move the right relationships forward.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Take ownership of a strong, existing events lineup for mortgage, primarily geared towards sales in-person meetings, and then building the playbook for expanding event presence on-stage, in new thought-leadership forums and through field motions.

 - Strategize a new non-real-estate events plan, including identifying strategic event and field motions in priority adjacent industries, designed to establish credibility, develop relationships, and create pipeline in those markets.

 - Unify existing and new vertical field marketing strategies into a tiered event strategy across industry, partner, customer, and executive programs.

 - Decide the right level of presence for each program, from attendance and executive meetings to sponsorships, booths, speaking opportunities, roundtables, dinners, and roadshows.

 - Run event programs end to end: goals, budget, registrations, vendors, booth and materials, attendee lists, on-site execution, and follow-up.

 - Partner with Lender and Settlement Sales to connect event plans to target accounts, meetings, and next steps, ensuring event participation converts into a repeatable pipeline and revenue motion, strengthens Snapdocs’ credibility across the mortgage ecosystem and new verticals, and builds executive, partner, and customer relationships that support growth

 - Work with Revenue Marketing on pre-event outreach, in-event signal capture, and post-event follow-up, including help with prospecting, messaging and social engagement.

 - Use HubSpot as the system of record for event planning, lists, activity tracking, and handoffs, with Salesforce and Slack connected where needed.

 - Track cost per attendee, meetings booked, meeting follow-up, qualified opportunities, pipeline impact, and 30-day post-event ROI. Use what you learn to make sharper investment calls.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of field marketing, event marketing, or go-to-market marketing experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, financial services, or a similarly complex industry.

 - A track record of owning events or field programs that contributed to qualified meetings, pipeline, customer relationships, or revenue.

 - Excellent project management. You keep many workstreams moving, write clear next steps, and make it obvious who owns what and when.

 - Strong judgment on event investment. You can assess attendee lists, audience fit, sponsorship value, sales goals, cost, and expected return before recommending a program.

 - Experience working closely with sales, customers, partners, vendors, and executives. You make it easy for others to do their part and keep things from falling through the cracks.

 - Comfort learning and operating marketing automation, CRM, lead capture, or event systems. Direct HubSpot experience is a plus.

 - Experience working on a lean marketing team with broad ownership, from deciding where to invest to making sure the room is ready.

 - Ability to travel to industry events, customer programs, and executive gatherings. Travel will be dependent on the specific event needs, but this role is not required to be at every event, instead using good judgment and clear evaluation of need to determine on-site presence levels.

AI PROFICIENCY AT SNAPDOCS

AI proficiency is a core expectation at Snapdocs. We expect you to use AI as part of your day-to-day work, with real judgment about where it helps and where you need to check the output.

For this role, that might include researching events, organizing event data, drafting outreach or briefs, building repeatable planning workflows, and connecting systems for regular check-ins and next steps for supporting partners. You should be curious about new uses, able to explain what changed in your work, and willing to verify what AI produces before it reaches a customer or sales team.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We believe in being upfront about pay. The base salary range for this role is as follows:

 - $131,000 - $150,000

Where you land within the range depends on your experience, skills, and how you'll make an impact in the role. In addition to base salary and variable compensation, this position includes meaningful equity and a comprehensive benefits package.

Why Snapdocs

We’re here to transform one of the most critical and complex industries in the world. That requires a team that is curious, driven, thoughtful, and practical. We value:

 - Product discipline and clear reasoning

 - Deep ownership of outcomes (not just tasks)

 - Straightforward, honest communication

 - Empathy for the people who use our software

This is a place for people who want to solve hard, meaningful problems with real economic impact — not just ship features.

JOIN US

We’re expanding our product suite and the network it connects. To do that, we need people who are excited by complexity, energized by scale, and motivated to make a tangible dent in how the mortgage ecosystem works. If you’re hungry to learn, build, and lead — you’ll do the best work of your career here.

To support our team, we offer a comprehensive & thoughtful benefits package for all full-time employees, which includes:

 Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

We are shaping the future of revenue intelligence and we want people who are excited to build what comes next. You will work with a team that dreams big, moves fast, and cares deeply about the craft and about each other. If you want to grow, stretch, and do work that truly matters, Gong is the place to do the best work of your career. Overview The GTM Compensation Leader owns the end-to-end strategy, design, and operations of sales compensation across the GTM organization. This role is the connective layer between RevOps, Finance, and Field leadership — translating business strategy into comp plans that drive the right behaviors, scale with the business, and hold up to audit and compliance scrutiny. You will lead a comp team, own the ICM/SPM platform, and be the primary voice on plan design, exception handling, and comp operations. 
 Core Responsibilities 
 Comp Plan Design & Strategy   
 
 Own the design of sales compensation plans across segments (Sales, CS/RA, SDR, Partnership, Solution Engineers and otherwhere applicable) — quota, accelerators, SPIFFs, and plan mechanics. 
 Translate GTM strategy (new logo, expansion, retention, Healthy ARR) into comp incentives that drive the intended rep behavior. 
 Partner with RevOps, GTM Leadership, and Finance to align comp design to business priorities each planning cycle. 
 
 Comp Operations & Exception Handling 
 
 Own end-to-end comp operations: crediting, calculations, payout accuracy, and dispute resolution. 
 Build scalable exception-handling logic and governance so one-off requests don't erode plan integrity. 
 Ensure timely, accurate payout cycles with clear audit trails. 
 
 ICM / SPM Platform Ownership :  
 
 Serve as the business owner for the ICM/SPM tool (e.g., Varicent, Everstage) — configuration, roadmap, and vendor relationship. 
 Lead or oversee implementation, migration, or optimization of the platform as the comp motion scales. 
 Ensure the platform reflects current plan logic with minimal manual workaround. 
 
 Compliance & Finance Partnership 
 
 Partner with Finance/Accounting to ensure comp expense recognition is compliant with ASC 606. 
 Own documentation and controls needed to support audit, SOX, and quarter/year-end close. 
 Ensure comp plan changes are properly evaluated for accounting and compliance impact before rollout. 
 
 Team Leadership 
 
 Lead and develop a sales compensation team; build a scalable operating model as headcount and plan complexity grow. 
 Set the bar for accuracy, responsiveness, and trust between the comp function and the field. 
 
 Change Management & Communication 
 
 Own communication and rollout of plan changes — clear, simple, and well-timed to the field. 
 Build feedback loops with field leadership to catch design issues early. 
 
 Scalable Systems & Governance 
 
 Build governance models (approval flows, exception thresholds, plan documentation standards) that scale without adding headcount. 
 Maintain a single source of truth for plan documents, rates, and quotas. 
 
 Key Qualifications 
 
 Experience leading a sales compensation team within a SaaS/tech environment 
 Hands-on experience implementing and/or owning an ICM or SPM tool — CaptivateIQ, Varicent or Everstage strongly preferred 
 Proven ownership of, and partnership across, comp plan design and comp operations 
 ASC 606 experience (comp expense recognition, accounting partnership) 
 Comfortable operating between strategy (plan design, GTM alignment) and execution (calculations, exceptions, payout accuracy) 
 Strong communication and change management skills — able to explain comp mechanics simply to the field 
 Based in NYC or Salt Lake City

 Mental Health benefits with covered therapy and coaching.

 Education & learning stipend for personal growth and development. 
 Flexible vacation time to promote a healthy work-life blend. 
 Paid parental leave to support you and your family. 
 Company-wide recharge days each quarter.

jobs.title: Group Product Marketing Manager
jobs.excerpt:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 

Vanta's Product Marketing team sits at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success. We define positioning and narrative for Vanta's platform, translate roadmap into go-to-market motions across big launch moments and releases, and make sure the field can sell what Product is building; with research, storytelling, and cross-functional partnership as the core of how we work.

About the role

AI is one of Vanta's most strategic bets, and it needs a dedicated owner. This PMM will be focused on bringing the AI roadmap to market in close partnership with EPD. You'll own the narrative, messaging, and positioning for Vanta’s AI story end-to-end, and be the connective tissue between what Engineering and Product are building and how the market, field, and customers understand it.

You're expected to shape our AI story and define Vanta as a leader in the space, which means you’re fast-moving and nimble, have enough technical fluency to have a real point of view in roadmap conversations with EPD (including getting hands-on and testing the product yourself), paired with the storytelling and creativity to bring a unique, differentiated story to market.

What you’ll do as a Product Marketing Manager at Vanta:

 - Own the AI pillar narrative and roadmap end to end

 - Own the AI pillar narrative at key events like VantaCon, including keynote support, breakout sessions, and customer testimonials

 - Ensure a cohesive AI narrative across pillars so AI messaging holds together whether it's showing up in Compliance, Risk, or Proof contexts

 - Partner directly with EPD to understand what's being built, influence roadmap sequencing from a market/customer lens, and translate technical capability into external-ready narrative

 - Develop and maintain AI messaging and positioning that flexes across audiences (field, analysts, press, customers)

 - Drive field enablement for AI, arming Sales and CS with the story, objection handling, and proof points they need

 - Plan and execute AI product launches, from planning through post-launch measurement

 - Represent the AI narrative in customer-facing and market-facing moments (analyst briefings, customer advisory conversations, press as needed)

How to be successful in this role:

 - Core PMM experience
 
 - 7+ years in product marketing, ideally with ownership of a full pillar or product line rather than a support function
 
 - Track record of building narrative and positioning from scratch, not just executing an existing playbook
 
 - Experience partnering directly with Product/Engineering leadership
 
 - Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
 
 - Plan and execute large product launches (including partnership with comms to align on product narrative), report back on performance, and optimize our launch processes for scale
 
 - Define and manage go-to-market (GTM) strategy for Vanta’s security products, including messaging, positioning, launch planning, GTM enablement content (sales, customer success), and customer adoption
 
 - Strong written and verbal storytelling, comfortable writing for a keynote stage as well as a sales deck
 
 - Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship

 Technical / AI fluency
 
 - Working understanding of how modern AI products are built, enough to ask sharp questions in an EPD roadmap review and push back credibly
 
 - Familiarity with the current AI/LLM landscape (model capabilities, common architecture patterns, where the industry conversation is headed) so positioning reflects real technical nuance rather than surface-level buzzwords
 
 - Comfort translating technical capability and constraints into narrative that's accurate and compelling without over-claiming what the product does
 
 - Prior experience marketing an AI-native or AI-adjacent product is a strong plus
 
 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

 Bonus points
 
 - Experience with security or technical products
 
 - Experience owning a keynote-level narrative for a company event
 
 - Background that spans both technical and brand/narrative work (e.g., came from a technical PM, solutions engineering, or technical writing background before moving into PMM)

What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans

 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office

 - Family planning benefits

 - Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting

 - Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time

 - 11 company-paid holidays

 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials. 

#LI-remote

At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.

About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role 
 The GTM Strategy & Operations, Frontier team coordinates how Anthropic's research reaches the market: how we run model launches commercially, how we partner with Capacity teams to allocate a finite compute supply across customers and surfaces, and how we translate what the field learns into reads that Research, Product, Finance, and GTM leadership act on. 
 One tangible example of the work this role will contribute to is new model and product introduction: the end-to-end commercial run of a model, product or capability release, from identifying market opportunities to preparing customer cohorts and the field through to the adoption readout that shapes where we go from there.  Run launches

 Synthesize customer adoption signal (usage patterns, migration behavior, qualitative feedback from the field) into actionable reads for executive leadership across the company 
 Design and run the field response loop: how AE, CS, Applied AI and customer response and feedback gets captured, triaged, and routed to the teams who can act on it 
 
 Evolve the NPI methodology 
 
 Design and iterate GTM's NPI methodology across both standard releases and managed-access programs, including operating cadence, roles and handoffs with field teams, and the bar for launch readiness 
 Carry the executive reporting cadence for launches: what leadership teams see, how often, and how we make adoption trends legible early as well as retrospectively in an continual sprint environment

jobs.title: Sales Operations Analyst
jobs.excerpt:
ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/ and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Clipboard is looking for a Sales Operations Analyst to help build and run the systems behind our sales organization.

You'll work across Salesforce, data, automation, and internal tools to help our sales team operate more effectively. That might mean building an automation that eliminates a recurring workflow, investigating a messy data problem, redesigning part of our Salesforce setup, or building a new system from the ground up.

We are a small team with an unusual operating model. Much of our execution runs through AI agents that we direct and quality-check, allowing each analyst to operate with the leverage of a much larger team.

This is equal parts builder and operator. You'll own systems end to end, work through ambiguous requests from reps and leadership, and be accountable for making sure the things you build actually work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own live systems. Take ownership of production systems such as account distribution, deal intelligence, competitor tracking, and data sync pipelines. You'll be accountable for their accuracy and reliability.

 - Solve ambiguous problems. Work through requests from sales reps, managers, and leadership, figure out what is actually needed, and execute quickly.

 - Direct AI agents. Write specs and prompts, supervise AI agents, and rigorously QA their output before it touches production data.

 - Build automations and tools. Create scripts, scheduled jobs, Slack bots, and lightweight web apps that turn recurring manual work into scalable systems.

 - Analyze and report. Use SQL and other tools to answer important revenue questions and build reporting the organization can trust.

 - Guard data quality. Handle merges, deduplication, account mapping, enrichment, and other work required to keep our systems accurate at scale.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Evidence of building. You've built scripts, automations, tools, systems, or other solutions to real problems.

 - AI-native working style. You already use AI to multiply your output and understand where it can fail and how to verify its work.

 - High judgment under ambiguity. You can take a loosely defined problem, figure out what matters, and know when to act versus when to ask.

 - Strong attention to detail. You're comfortable being the last line of defense before changes affect production systems and large datasets.

 - Bias to ownership. When something you own breaks, you don't just fix the immediate issue. You look for the underlying problem and improve the system.

SQL and Python experience are strong pluses, but we're more interested in your curiosity, judgment, and ability to ship than checking every technical box.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Salesforce administration or development experience, including flows, SOQL, or data model design.

 - Experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Operations, analytics, or a similar environment.

 - Experience building automations with tools, scripts, APIs, or AI agents.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. Application Review – We'll review your experience and evidence of things you've built, automated, or owned.

 2. Take-Home Assessment – A practical, ~2-hour assessment using a fictional company, mock website, and CRM. You'll have 48 hours to complete it, and AI tools are encouraged.

 3. Technical Walkthrough – A 45-minute session where you'll demo what you built, explain your decisions, and make a small live change to your system.

 4. Manager Interview – A 30-minute conversation focused on communication, ownership, judgment, and how you operate under ambiguity.

 5. Final Steps / Offer! – Some candidates may have an executive conversation, followed by references and an offer.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive base salary

 - Insurance benefits + 401k options

 - Unlimited PTO and flexible holidays

 - Remote-first working environment

To get a better understanding of the general type of people we want to hire, you can check out our blog here. https://creatingvalue.substack.com/

Quick Note on Scammers: 

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6.

jobs.excerpt:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role 
 This is a partner marketing role that demands product marketing craft. You'll be the single-threaded owner of how every Claude launch lands on partner marketing surfaces. We reach many of our most important customers through our partners. When we ship a new model or capability, it doesn't just launch on first-party surfaces; it launches across our growing partner ecosystem, each with their own product pages, blogs, seller enablement, and go-to-market motions. Our product release cadence has accelerated, and we're looking for someone to own that translation end-to-end. 
 Model and capabilities launches are the core of the job and the majority of the work. The rest is solution launches — the joint and co-built solutions that land on partner surfaces alongside our models. The two halves reinforce each other. Model launches create the moment; solution launches translate what’s possible for the sellers and customers on the other side. 
 You'll be the first dedicated owner of launch readiness across our partner surfaces, consolidating work currently spread across several people and creating a center of excellence for how we do this work. This role centralizes launch coordination for our partners — briefing partner teams under confidentiality, shaping how our positioning shows up on their surfaces, and orchestrating execution cross functionally. You'll be the person who knows exactly what's available on which surface, how we're messaging it, and how it all fits together. You will use this knowledge to ensure our launches are positioned for the highest impact and amplification across our partners. 
 The job is roughly half launch execution and half building. On the execution side, you'll run the launch playbook. On the building side, you'll define what we haven't had the bandwidth to create yet. You'll set the standard for how Anthropic shows up on partner surfaces and hold the rest of the company to it, without anyone involved reporting to you. 
 Anthropic reaches a substantial share of its customer base through partner surfaces, and the ecosystem is still growing. How Claude shows up on the platforms where enterprises actually buy AI is largely unwritten. This is the role that writes it. 
 Responsibilities 

 Own partner launch readiness end-to-end, serving as the directly responsible individual for every model, feature, and solution launch across the partner ecosystem — from the first briefing through launch-day go-live and reach reporting 

 Define the operating model for partner launches: set the standard for what readiness means, decide what's durable enough to share and when, and own the trade-offs when timelines and partner needs conflict 

 Equip partner sellers and solution architects to position Claude for a customer workload without escalating to us — segment-specific enablement, technical content, and the materials their field actually reaches for 

 Translate Anthropic positioning for partner surfaces, taking source messaging from Product Marketing and creating partner-specific versions that account for what's available where, what each partner needs to hear, and how the narrative lands on their platform 

 Own the go-to-market motion for joint and co-built solutions on partner surfaces — position what a partner and Anthropic have built together, make the value legible to that partner's sellers and customers, and land it across the channels where their buyers look 

 Work with Partnerships, Product, and partner-side teams to shape solutions into launchable moments, and make the call on which are worth a launch at all 

 Run launch execution – Manage cross-functional review cycles, support partner launch preparedness, compile post-launch reporting 

 Build post-launch momentum through partner webinars, technical content pipelines, and campaigns that keep partners selling after launch-day 

 Represent the partner perspective internally — surface Anthropic-direct launches that will affect partner relationships, flag partner-experience issues in product decisions, and make sure partner considerations arrive early rather than as a fire drill 

 Turn informal knowledge into documented, repeatable process as our release cadence and partner portfolio grow, and build the function so it scales beyond any one person

 Have done partner marketing or product marketing work for or on cloud AI/ML platforms — positioning products on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, or directly comparable surfaces, whether from inside a cloud provider or as an independent software vendor launching on one

 Can drive cross-functional work without direct authority, pushing internal teams and external partner organizations toward deadlines while keeping the relationships intact, in fast-moving environments where dates move and information is incomplete

 Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

About Gusto 
 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. 
   All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers.  About the Role 
 This is your chance to shape the foundation of a fast-growing, high-impact part of Gusto's business as a Senior Sales Operations Analyst supporting our Expansion Sales organization. You'll build the insights and AI-powered solutions that make a large, multi-team sales organization more productive — spanning our Platform Sales, Expansion AM, and New Expansion Advisor teams. You'll sit at the intersection of data, process, and execution; you'll turn real sales challenges into the tools, reports, automations, and workflows that move the numbers. 
 You'll help grow revenue from Gusto's existing customer base through upsells and cross-sells. If you thrive where analytics, problem-solving, and supporting others meet, this role offers ownership, visibility, and the chance to influence how Gusto expands its relationship with the small businesses it already serves. 
 About the Team 
 The Expansion Sales Operations team partners closely with sales leadership to support three dynamic, fast-moving sales teams that contribute meaningfully to Gusto's growth. We think of ourselves as builders, problem solvers, and strategic partners; we turn uncertainty into clarity and fragmented processes into scalable, repeatable systems. 
 Our work spans pacing and pipeline forecasting, quotas, trigger and backlog management, process design, data integrity, account and territory administration, rules of engagement, and increasingly, AI-driven optimization. We value curiosity, open communication, and a commitment to helping our reps operate efficiently and confidently across a multi-product, multi-team motion. 
 Here's what you'll do day-to-day 
 Analytics, Reporting & Forecasting 
 
 Build, automate, and maintain reports and dashboards that track pacing, funnel metrics, trigger and backlog health, SLAs, and rep productivity; keep definitions consistent and documentation clear. 
 Own the weekly forecast, CFQ closed-won ARR pacing, and probability-weighted pipeline forecast, feeding the Weekly Business Review (WBR) and Weekly Forecast Review (WFR) cadence for sales and executive leadership. 
 Partner with Finance and Analytics to produce operational reporting and revenue insights across dials, connects, lead passes, self-generated opportunities, and book coverage. 
 Own metric definitions and data accuracy so leaders trust the numbers they act on. 
 
 Drive AI Strategy for Sales 
 
 Identify and prototype AI and automation tools, such as process automation, analytics copilots, and call coaching, that remove manual friction from the sales process. 
 Partner with Sales, BizTech, Product, and Enablement to embed AI into daily sales workflows, improving both efficiency and effectiveness. 
 Source and lead net-new AI and automation projects, connecting data insights to process improvements that lift rep productivity. 
 
 Process Design & Continuous Improvement 
 
 Examine workflows and rep performance to identify bottlenecks; recommend and implement process and automation changes that improve conversion, efficiency, and the rep experience. 
 Evaluate Rules of Engagement (ROE) requests and comp exception asks, applying clear rules and precedent to produce fair, consistent, and binding rulings. 
 Partner with Sales Enablement to document processes, build playbooks, and drive adoption of new tools and workflows. 
 
 Operational Support & Problem-Solving 
 
 Provide day-to-day support to Expansion Sales leadership and reps: ad hoc data requests, process issues, and one-off investigations. 
 Own account and territory administration as the business evolves: assignment and coverage upkeep, book reassignments for leave and departures, large-scale account rerouting, and segment reclassification, supported by lead-routing and round-robin (ChiliPiper) automation. 
 Support onboarding and offboarding for new hires and departing reps, including roster updates, router mapping, and leave-of-absence (LOA) processing. 
 Troubleshoot reporting issues, broken workflows, missing CRM data, and gaps in pipeline visibility with fast, accurate fixes — including closed-won opportunities that didn't sync and ARR discrepancies. 
 
 Cross-Functional Partnership & Communication 
 
 Work closely with Sales Leadership, RevOps, Finance, BizTech, and Product to keep everyone aligned and remove obstacles to progress. 
 Translate sales challenges into clear business requirements; partner cross-functionally to design solutions and durable improvements. 
 Keep stakeholders aligned with clear, regular updates to managers and senior leadership on timelines, risks, and outcomes. 
 Act as a trusted advisor, bringing structure, insight, and clarity to complex or ambiguous problems. 
 
 Here's what we're looking for 
 
 5+ years in Sales Ops, RevOps, or a similar analytical GTM role; ideally in a fast-paced SaaS or fintech environment. 
 Strong Salesforce proficiency; you can spot data issues, audit pipeline problems, manage account ownership and routing, and build reports and dashboards that reps and leaders actually use. 
 Analytical depth across Salesforce reports and dashboards, SQL, Tableau or Looker, and Excel/Google Sheets. 
 Hands-on experience with forecasting, pipeline management, and territory or quota planning on a recurring cadence; for example, a weekly forecast feeding monthly reviews and QBRs. 
 Comfort evaluating AI and automation tools and prototyping simple workflows to improve productivity. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication; you simplify complex information and create alignment from frontline reps to senior directors. 
 A first-principles problem solver who breaks down ambiguous issues, tests hypotheses, and builds structured solutions. 
 Exceptionally organized and detail-oriented, you manage multiple projects and recurring workflows while protecting data quality and operational reliability. 
 A strong partner to sales, with a track record supporting teams that have competing, fast-changing priorities. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 
 Experience supporting an expansion, upsell, or cross-sell motion into an existing customer base, rather than net-new acquisition.

You will translate business goals and the North America operating plan into measurable, multi-channel marketing programs that support revenue growth, , using business priorities and performance insights to shape campaign strategy and make informed recommendations. To bring these to life, you will partner closely with the Sales, Product Marketing, Product and Business Operations teams.

About Gusto 
 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers.    AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. About the Role 
 This is your chance to shape the foundation of a fast-growing, high-impact part of Gusto's business as a Senior Sales Operations Analyst supporting our Health Insurance (HI) Sales team. You'll sit at the intersection of data, process, and execution; you'll turn real sales challenges into the tools, reports, automations, and workflows that move the numbers. 
 You'll help grow a business segment that serves tens of thousands of small businesses through smarter, data-driven sales strategies. If you thrive where analytics, problem-solving, and supporting others meet, this role offers ownership, visibility, and the chance to influence how Gusto sells health insurance. 
 About the Team 
 The HI Sales Operations team partners closely with sales leadership to support two dynamic, fast-moving sales teams that contribute meaningfully to Gusto's growth. We think of ourselves as builders, problem solvers, and strategic partners; we turn uncertainty into clarity and fragmented processes into scalable, repeatable systems. 
 Our work spans quotas, pipeline health, forecasting, process design, data integrity, account and territory administration, go-to-market strategy, and increasingly, AI-driven optimization. We value curiosity, open communication, and a commitment to helping 80+ sales reps operate efficiently and confidently.

 Analytics, Reporting & Forecasting 
 
 Build, automate, and maintain reports and dashboards that track sales performance, funnel metrics, pipeline health, SLAs, and rep productivity; keep definitions consistent and documentation clear. 
 Partner with RevOps, Finance, Marketing, and Analytics to produce operational reporting, revenue insights, and forecasting models across the weekly forecast, monthly reviews, and QBR cadence. 
 Own metric definitions and data accuracy so leaders trust the numbers they act on. 
 
 Drive AI Strategy for Sales 
 
 Identify and prototype AI and automation tools, such as content generation, analytics copilots, and call coaching, that remove manual friction from the sales process. 
 Partner with Sales, BizTech, Product, and Enablement to embed AI into daily sales workflows, improving both efficiency and effectiveness. 
 Source and lead net-new AI and automation projects, connecting data insights to process improvements that lift rep productivity. 
 
 Process Design & Continuous Improvement 
 
 Examine workflows and rep performance to identify bottlenecks; recommend and implement process and automation changes that improve conversion, efficiency, and the rep experience. 
 Partner with Sales Enablement to document processes, build playbooks, and drive adoption of new tools and workflows. 
 
 Operational Support & Problem-Solving 
 
 Provide day-to-day support to HI Sales leadership and reps: ad hoc data requests, process issues, and one-off investigations. 
 Own account and territory administration as the business evolves, assignment and coverage upkeep, book reassignments for leave and departures, large-scale account rerouting, and segment reclassification, supported by lead-routing and round-robin automation. 
 Support territory, quota, and coverage planning, plus monthly sales-compensation reconciliation. 
 Troubleshoot reporting issues, broken workflows, missing CRM data, and gaps in pipeline visibility with fast, accurate fixes. 
 
 Cross-Functional Partnership & Communication 
 
 Work closely with Sales Leadership, RevOps, Finance, BizTech, and Product to keep everyone aligned and remove obstacles to progress. 
 Translate sales challenges into clear business requirements; partner cross-functionally to design solutions and durable improvements. 
 Keep stakeholders aligned with clear, regular updates to managers and senior leadership on timelines, risks, and outcomes.

 5+ years in Sales Ops, RevOps, or a similar analytical GTM role; ideally in a fast-paced SaaS or fintech environment.

 Hands-on experience with forecasting, pipeline management, and territory or quota planning on a recurring cadence; for example, a weekly forecast feeding monthly reviews and QBRs.

 Excellent written and verbal communication; you simplify complex information and create alignment from frontline reps to senior directors. 
 A first-principles problem solver who breaks down ambiguous issues, tests hypotheses, and builds structured solutions.

 A strong partner to sales, with a track record supporting teams that have competing, fast-changing priorities.

 Experience supporting a regulated or compliance-driven sales segment such as health insurance or benefits. 
 Experience designing or implementing automations, AI workflows, or similar tooling. 
 A track record of building cross-functional relationships across Sales, BizTech, and Analytics.

We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. This is one of the biggest growth opportunities in the business and one of the least-covered by traditional demand gen. 
 This is not a "run the playbook" role. We expect this person to build with AI as a default — designing agentic workflows that scale programs beyond what headcount alone could, and pushing the team forward on how demand gen should operate in 2026 and beyond. 
 You'd be joining a demand gen team that is genuinely rebuilding how the function works — where AI agents run real production programs, and where the people on the team design the machine rather than turn the crank. If you want to define what a demand gen career looks like in the agentic era, this is the seat to do it from. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 
 Own customer lifecycle demand gen. Build and run programs that create demand inside our existing customer base — expansion, cross-sell, and adoption plays across email, in-app, web, and field channels, in partnership with sales and customer teams. 
 Work across channels, not in one. Support and strengthen programs across paid, email, events, web, and outbound as team priorities shift. You'll be the person who can step into any channel and make the program better. 
 Build agentic workflows. Use AI tools (Claude Code, agents, internal AI infrastructure) to automate program execution — audience building, content generation, signal detection, campaign QA — and treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not a side project.

 What Makes You a Great Fit

 Hands-on with AI in your actual work: you've built automations or agentic workflows (or are visibly on that path), and you think about AI as leverage, not a threat or a buzzword.

 Familiarity with the observability / monitoring / open source ecosystem.

 You've written or shipped something public about AI in marketing operations.

 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring.  As a Sales Development Representative (SDR), you will focus on three core missions.  One, you will help our users and prospects navigate their Grafana journey by engaging with and listening to them in order to provide them with appropriate resources and guidance.  Two, with these learnings, you will partner with our Sales Team to connect with other influential people in these organizations to identify new business opportunities that are the pipeline for our company’s revenue goals by partnering proactively with our Sales Team. And three, you will develop valuable, transferable skills to help you achieve your career goals.  By fulfilling our three core  missions, you will contribute importantly to Grafana Labs’ community and business goals.   
 We understand that our commercial success is linked to our open source DNA and users’ success with our software.  As such, we want team members who can effectively leverage this connection and help support the long-term health of our company. 
 In this role, you will balance reactive and proactive work, responding to inbound inquiries as well as outreaching to target accounts. You will need to research and have a detective mindset in order to craft thoughtful, value-add messaging; and you’ll need to be confident driving business conversations on the phone.  You will need to know how to use AI as a tool to constantly improve your productivity.  
 This is a demanding and rewarding role.   It is a fast-paced and challenging environment.  While our company is growing sustainably,  we still have a lot of building and improving to do.  And we do this work together with our teammates from more than 15 different countries.  We're looking for driven, humble, technically curious  people who embrace a team-first attitude and demonstrate extreme ownership.   This is a great team to join, whether you’re just starting your career or looking to pivot into the tech industry.  You’ll have managers and teammates that care deeply about you as a professional and human, and you will learn more than you thought possible. 
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 
 Build and maintain knowledge of our technology, competitors, open source ecosystem, and industry trends 
 Follow up on inbound leads effectively and efficiently 
 Use a multi-channel approach (email, social, calling) to proactively outreach to new leads within target accounts; our top SDRs are confident and effective on the phone 
 Use Salesforce and Grafana dashboards for lead and account management and research 
 Use research and data to prioritize and customize outreach to target prospects and accounts via email and LinkedIn 
 Drive effective discovery conversations to understand users’ needs and goals in to provide them the appropriate resources and communicate how Grafana can help them  
 Consistently meet new business opportunity and pipeline targets 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams such as marketing and sales to win as a team 
 
 What Makes You a Great Fit: 
 
 Located in NORAM 
 Open to feedback and coaching, always looking for ways to improve  
 Clear and concise written and verbal communication style 
 Excellent organizational skills and the ability to prioritize many tasks and demands 
 Willingness and ability to take on any task - no matter how small or big - with a focus on quality 
 Resourceful and proactive in an environment that is constantly evolving 
 Driven by purpose and by winning with a team-first attitude 
 
 Bonus Points For: 
   
 Let’s be honest - interviewing is not easy. However, we want you to come prepared and succeed. When we interview, we’re trying to determine a couple of things: 

 Would you be successful if you were part of our team? 
 Will you love working here and be a positive influence on your fellow colleagues? 
 Will you grow professionally and personally during your time here? 
 We’re looking for people who are curious and passionate about technology, so make sure you invest some time in learning about Grafana Labs. Explore our community, the industry we operate in, what we offer, and how we set ourselves apart. 
 During your interview, you’ll be sharing stories about your current and past roles and experiences. The best way to frame this is with the CARR model: Context, Action, Results, Reflection. This allows you to succinctly share the experiences you’ve gained. 
 Remember, humility drives learning and we love working with people who are always trying to better themselves. Throughout our interview process, you will receive feedback, and usually directly in the interview. As you move through the interview process, make sure you listen to the feedback you receive and figure out how to incorporate the advice in the next step of the interview.  

 Compensation & Rewards 
 In the United States, the OTE compensation range for this role is $ 80,750 - $83,650 .  Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable) and other benefits listed  here . 
 
 *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

 100% Remote, Global Culture -  As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.

Who we are 
 At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years. 
 What we do 
 The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. We have a people-first culture that fosters kindness, collaboration, and innovation, and empowers our Gurus with tools to fuel their career growth. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride! Role overview 
 The Brand Marketing Manager will work directly with the Sr. Director of Brand Marketing to oversee brand campaigns, content creation, and sponsorships across the US, CA, and UK — managing strategy, execution, and performance. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Lead integrated brand campaigns across US, CA, and UK — from brief to launch — partnering with PR, product marketing, and media teams across TV, CTV, OOH, audio, influencer, social, and sponsorships. 
 Write insight-led creative briefs that clearly define audience, objectives, messaging, and success metrics.

Visit klaviyo.com/careers  to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny. About the Role 
 Klaviyo is building the operating system for consumer businesses. Behind every sales motion, every account handoff, and every renewal is a product ecosystem that either accelerates or constrains growth. This role exists to ensure our GTM Sales systems are an accelerant. 
 The Product Owner for GTM Sales Systems (Accounts & Opportunities) is a strategic and executional leader who owns the product vision, roadmap, and delivery for how Klaviyo manages its most foundational sales domains: Accounts and Opportunities. You will define how sellers interact with account data, how opportunity workflows drive deal velocity, and how the systems and processes that underpin these domains evolve to meet the demands of a rapidly scaling enterprise GTM motion. The platform today is Salesforce, but the thinking is not constrained by any single tool. You are designing the right experience and architecture first, then determining how to deliver it. 
 This is not a systems administration role. You are a product owner who happens to operate in the GTM technology space. You will write product requirements, define success metrics, drive discovery, own sprint prioritization, and deliver outcomes that move business KPIs. Critically, you will approach every workflow with an AI-first mindset: mapping processes, categorizing what should be human-led versus AI-augmented versus AI-automated, and redesigning how work gets done rather than layering AI onto broken processes. You report into the GTS Product Owner team, which sits within the CIO organization and is accountable for product strategy across all GTM business systems. 
 Who You Are 
 You think in systems, not tickets. You see an Account and think about data architecture, seller workflows, and downstream analytics. You see an Opportunity and think about pipeline velocity, conversion rates, and forecast accuracy. When you encounter a manual process, your instinct is to ask whether AI should be doing this, not how to make the manual version faster. You are equally comfortable presenting a product vision to a CRO and writing acceptance criteria for a sprint. You have deep CRM expertise, but you do not let any single platform define the boundaries of your product thinking.

 Qualifications
